claims.statement: Poland had about 11,762 publicly accessible charging points at the end of 2025, up 36% year over year, including about 4,400 DC points.
AFIR requires public chargers to support specified ad-hoc payment practices and requires free static and dynamic data including operational status, availability, and price through APIs.
Those public data create an unusually concrete outage-led prospecting trigger, but data quality, owner identification, and willingness to outsource operations remain unproven.

contrary_evidence: Large CPOs already operate network operations centers and may view an external layer as added failure risk.
Hardware warranties, closed backends, and payment-provider dependencies can prevent remote resolution.
Regulatory data obligations do not themselves establish a standardized commercial uptime SLA or prove loss per outage.

economics.acquisition_route: Continuously analyze the mandatory public operational-status feeds to identify fleets with recurring visible outages, send the responsible owner a quantified diagnostic sample, and convert to a paid monitored pilot. Separately, let charger installers embed the desk in every handover so they can sell an SLA without building a round-the-clock operations team.
economics.founder_time: Part-time validation hypothesis; delivery burden remains untested.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Vendor-specific remote-remedy playbooks, reliable backend integrations, regional dispatch coverage, parts staging, and measured first-response and first-time-fix performance compound together. Route and technician density improve margins beyond what monitoring software alone can deliver.
fingerprint.customer: Regional charge-point operators and retail, hotel, parking, fleet, or municipal site owners operating 20-500 mixed-brand public chargers in Poland and nearby CEE markets.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Continuously analyze the mandatory public operational-status feeds to identify fleets with recurring visible outages, send the responsible owner a quantified diagnostic sample, and convert to a paid monitored pilot. Separately, let charger installers embed the desk in every handover so they can sell an SLA without building a round-the-clock operations team.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Connect to OCPP/backend feeds and required public status data, attempt safe remote remedies, classify faults, maintain payment and API evidence, and dispatch the correct qualified technician with parts context. Start as a managed network-operations service and automate the common faults; do not pretend that adding software later automatically removes field-service constraints.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The fleet owner pays a recurring fee per connector for monitoring, remote triage, data-quality compliance, and ticket management, plus a pre-agreed coordination fee for each field repair; payment recurs monthly against a transparent service report.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A charger reports out-of-order, repeated payment or session failures breach a site SLA, AFIR data are stale, or a property owner cannot determine whether the fault belongs to connectivity, backend, payment, power, or hardware.

founder_fit: Matches data engineering, anomaly detection, automation, and the founder's renewable-installation adjacency.
A small pilot is capital-light if field work is contracted and spare-parts inventory is avoided initially.
Operational escalation can become time-intensive, so a narrow fleet size and business-hours SLA are important while the founder remains employed.
risks: Evidence of a workflow, transition, or loss does not yet establish recurring willingness to pay.
The proposed distribution and compounding mechanisms remain hypotheses pending buyer evidence.

title: Vendor-Neutral EV Charger Reliability Operations
uncertainties: Share of Polish endpoints exposing accurate status and the legal entity behind each fleet.
OCPP/backend access rates across charger brands and safe remote actions allowed by owners.
Technician travel cost, parts delay, and gross margin at different fleet densities.
Pricing, buyer authority, and acquisition economics remain unvalidated at discovery.

First validation test: Monitor 300 public connectors across at least five operators for 30 days, manually verify a sample of reported outages, and send ten evidence-based fleet reports. Require one paid 50-connector pilot with backend access and predefined response metrics; continue only if at least 60% of tickets can be closed remotely or in one field visit at positive contribution margin.
